Sanjay Vashisth, J. (Oral)
1.

The instant petition has been filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (earlier Section 439 Cr.P.C.),
for grant of regular bail to the petitioner, during the pendency of trial, who has been booked in a criminal case arising out of First Information Report, as detailed here-under:-
IName of FIR [Date Section(s) Police Station [District Petitioner(s) INo.
Sajan 168 27.07.2025 21, 27(a), 29, 61 and 85 ofJandiala [Amritsar INDPS Act, Rural 2.

As per allegations, recovery of 10.15 grams of heroin was affected from the transparent polythene bag carried by Kajal along with Rs.1200/- as drug money and from co-accused Sarabjit Kaur Rs.1900/- as drug money from the spot on 27.07.2025.

Subsequently, on the basis of disclosure statement of main accused -- Kajal, name of the petitioner was involved in the case by alleging that the said contraband weighing 10.15 grams of heroin was supplied by the present petitioner.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner argues that except of the integrity of this document PHHC,
Chandigarh LAVISHA 2025.11.06 19:16 ge ie alleged disclosure statement, which in fact is a very weak evidence, no other substantive evidence has been collected by the prosecution during the course of investigation to prove the involvement of the petitioner in the present case.
Further submits that petitioner is inside jail since 29.07.2025, i.e., for the last about more than 03 months.

Besides, submits that earlier petitioner was found indulged in case FIR No. 221, dated Sajan vs State Of Punjab on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165482809/
1 16.07.2020, under Sections 376, 343, 354-A of IPC and Sections 4 & 6 of POCSO Act, registered at PS Jandiala, District Amritsar.
However, in that case too, he was acquitted vide judgment dated 25.01.2024.
Except this, petitioner is not involved in any other case of similar nature.
4. Additionally, learned counsel points out that trial is yet to commence and thus, statements of prosecution witnesses have yet to be recorded.
Therefore, continued incarceration of the petitioner in such circumstances, is not going to serve any useful purpose.
Thus, he prays for grant of concession of regular bail to the petitioner.
5. On the other hand, learned State Counsel has filed the custody certificate dated 03.11.2025in Court today, which is taken on record, subject to all just exceptions.
Office to tag the same at appropriate place.

A copy thereof has been handed over to the counsel for the petitioner.
6.
Learned State counsel while vehemently opposing the prayer for bail, submits that the alleged offence is grave in nature and falls under the ambit of Section 37(1)(b) of NDPS Act.

Besides, present petitioner is involved in drug trafficking, which is also a menace for the | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document PHHC, Chandigarh LAVISHA 2025.11.06 19:16 society more particular the youth of the society.
It is also argued that the offences under the NDPS Act have serious social ramifications and releasing the petitioner at this stage may send a wrong signal to the people at large in the society.
It is further urged that petitioner's release on bail may hamper the fair progress of trial and thus, prays for dismissal of the bail petition.

7. Having considered the rival submissions and perused the material on record, this Court finds that no recovery has been effected from the petitioner, and his alleged implication rests solely upon the disclosure statement of a co-accused, which, in isolation, does not constitute substantive evidence and is otherwise inadmissible in law.

At this stage, there appear reasonable grounds to believe that the petitioner may not be guilty of the alleged offence until the prosecution establishes its case by leading cogent evidence before the trial Court.
The petitioner has remained in custody for over three months, the trial is yet to commence, and no other case of similar nature is shown against him.

Therefore, taking into consideration the totality of the facts and circumstances, the nature of allegations, and the period of custody already undergone, this Court deems it appropriate to grant the concession of regular bail to the petitioner.
Consequently, prayer made in the present petition is allowed.

Petitioner is ordered to be released on bail, subject to his furnishing bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court/ Chief Judicial Magistrate/ Illaqa Magistrate/ Duty Magistrate concerned, if not required in any other case.
